name: Vanthorpe Meridian Blazer
description:
Vanthorpe's answer to the question of what a corporate professional wears when the meeting isn't formal enough for a suit but casual isn't acceptable. The Meridian Blazer is a single-breasted two-button in a medium-weight wool-poly blend available in charcoal, navy, and a dark forest that reads almost black in poor light. The construction is half-canvassed — more structure than a dress blazer, less than a suit jacket — and the lapels are a modest notch cut that doesn't date quickly. Interior pockets are deep and numerous, a Vanthorpe signature. The lining is a deep burgundy silk-analog that shows only when the jacket opens.

This is the jacket that Tier 3 professionals live in. It goes over a dress shirt for a client meeting and over a henley for a working lunch. It's been carefully designed to communicate that the wearer is serious without being ostentatious, which is exactly the register that Tier 3 corporate culture requires. Tier 4 buyers occasionally pick it up as a casual alternative to their bespoke pieces. It is not an exciting jacket. It is a jacket that works every day for years.
what_it_says: You're competent, reliable, and you understand what the room expects of you.
worn_by: people interviewing for the next tier
story_hooks: A blazer left in a conference room after a late meeting contains a folded note in the interior pocket — handwritten, in a cipher, addressed to no one.
Someone has been attending Tier 4 corporate events in a Meridian Blazer, passing as an analyst; they've been doing it for months and nobody has caught them.
The burgundy lining of a specific production batch was dyed with a compound that reacts faintly to a particular scanner frequency — nobody at Vanthorpe will say why.
